notes: WEAKEST CHECK IN THE GUARD. Pattern lists are brittle by construction and
an attacker who can read this file can trivially phrase around it.
Therefore injection_phrasing is listed in GuardConfig.weak_checks and is
capped at 'medium': it can never, on its own, produce a BLOCK. It exists
to label text for ingress neutralization and to give the dashboard
something to show, not to carry the defense.
Structural checks (hit_test, invisible_text, cross_origin_form) are what
actually stop attacks. This file is extensible at run time: point
GUARD_INJECTION_PATTERNS at another JSON file with the same shape.

patterns.description: Attempts to redefine the agent's role.
Forged conversation turn or chat-template delimiter embedded in page text.
Text explicitly addressed to a model rather than to a human reader.

patterns.regex: \b(security (scanner|review|audit)|verified safe|approved by (the )?(guard|security|admin)|compliance check passed|this page (is|has been) (verified|approved|whitelisted)|safety (check|scan) (passed|complete))\b
patterns.description: Claims of prior approval aimed at a guard or reviewer. This is the exact attack our architecture is designed to be immune to: L3 cannot clear a finding, so text like this can only ever add suspicion.

patterns.regex: \b(do not (tell|mention|inform|reveal)|without (telling|informing|asking)|don'?t (mention|disclose)|keep this (secret|hidden|between us)|silently|no need to (confirm|ask))\b[^.\n]{0,40}\b(user|human|owner|operator|them)\b|\b(do not|don'?t) (show|display|surface) this\b
patterns.description: Instructs the agent to conceal something from its principal.
Imperative addressed at whoever is reading, pushing a state-changing action. Low on its own: ordinary retail copy says 'please click Checkout'.
Solicits a secret. Pairs with the exfiltration policy rule in L2.
Text addressed at the defensive layer itself.

patterns.regex: \b(urgent|immediately|right now|before it'?s too late|last chance|expires in|act now)\b[^.\n]{0,40}\b(confirm|accept|subscribe|pay|order|upgrade|continue)\b
patterns.description: Pressure phrasing. Very common in benign marketing copy - deliberately low severity.
